subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a current in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n: a sequentially continuous linear functional on the space 𝒟ⁿ(U) of smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The support of S is spt S = U ∖ Z_S, where Z_S is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11, as formalized by GeometricCurrentOn.support). If tsupport ω ∩ spt S = ∅, then S(ω) = 0. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by the selected parent itself, in step 0(e) and hence in steps 2 and 4: (S − C)(ιω) = 0 when tsupport ω misses spt(S − C), and Ŷ(ιω) = 0 when tsupport ω misses spt Ŷ. Its audited proof follows.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 2.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–301) and the standard partition-of-unity argument; Simon uses this property tacitly (e.g. in 2.12). Write 𝒲 for the family of open sets W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S vanishing on W (S(η) = 0 whenever η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport η ⊆ W); thus Z_S = ⋃𝒲 and spt S = U ∖ Z_S.
1. Since ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω is smooth with compact support, so C := tsupport ω is compact, and C ⊆ U. If C = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume C ≠ ∅.
2. From C ⊆ U and C ∩ (U ∖ Z_S) = ∅ we get C ⊆ Z_S = ⋃𝒲. The members of 𝒲 are open and C is compact, so there are W_1, …, W_N ∈ 𝒲 with C ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_N.
3. Choose a smooth partition of unity on the compact (hence closed) set C subordinate to the open cover (W_i)_{i≤N}: C^∞ functions χ_1, …, χ_N : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport χ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_{i=1}^N χ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ C. (Such partitions exist on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, e.g. Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), or directly from smooth bump functions, Mathlib exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset.)
4. For each i put ω_i := χ_i ω, i.e. ω_i(x) = χ_i(x)·ω(x). Then ω_i is smooth and tsupport ω_i ⊆ tsupport χ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ C. Hence tsupport ω_i is compact and contained in U, so ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and tsupport ω_i ⊆ W_i with W_i ∈ 𝒲, so S(ω_i) = 0.
5. Σ_{i=1}^N ω_i = ω pointwise: for x ∈ C, Σ_i χ_i(x)ω(x) = ω(x); for x ∉ C, ω(x) = 0 and hence ω_i(x) = 0 for all i. By linearity of S on 𝒟ⁿ(U), S(ω) = Σ_{i=1}^N S(ω_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U missing spt S = U ∖ Z_S, so finitely many open W_i (closure compact in U) on which S vanishes cover it.
A smooth partition of unity χ_i on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i splits ω = Σ χ_i ω, each χ_i ω a test form in U supported in W_i.
S(χ_i ω) = 0 for each i, hence S(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12) — reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used, through part (i), by compact_sum_bound (step 1) and by the selected parent in steps 0(a), 1, 2, 3 and 5. Its audited proof follows.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 2.11–2.12. Notation: μ := μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm; I strictly increasing multi-indices), dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}, ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α).
1. Where R.orients holds at x ∈ M (Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so μ-a.e.), ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = s·Σ_I α(e_I)det(τ^I) with τ orthonormal, s = ±1 (multilinearity, alternation; τ^I = rows I of the matrix of τ), and Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet). So |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Schwarz), and ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), so |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ (n = 0: I = ∅, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1). ξ^♭ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous linear in ξ; R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: a.e. strongly measurable, zero off the compact spt ω ⊆ U, a.e. bounded by θ·sup|ω| (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). So T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩dμ.
3. For open W and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), ⟨ω, ξ⟩ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. (step 1) and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ(W) (step 2). So M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. For real t < μ(W) (μ(W) = ∞ allowed) we find admissible ω with T(ω) > t. G := W ∩ U is open and σ-compact, μ(G) = μ(W) (M ⊆ U), and μ, finite on compacts of U, is Radon on G (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15): inner regular by compacts, outer regular on finite-measure sets. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon 1.17): a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < η, ξ^♭|K' continuous, |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ μ-a.e. on K'. (b) An open V ⊇ K' with V̄ ⊆ G compact, μ(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend ξ^♭|K' coefficientwise continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), retract radially onto the closed |·|-unit ball of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), multiply by a continuous χ: ℝ^P → [0, 1], χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V: g is continuous, spt g ⊆ V compact, |g| ≤ 1, g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise, standard mollifier): for 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V) it is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)|dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_ε → g uniformly; so g_ε is admissible. (e) With δ_ε := sup|g_ε − g|·μ(V̄) → 0 (μ(V̄) < ∞), steps 2, 1 give T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩dμ ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩dμ − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩|dμ − δ_ε ≥ μ(K') − η − δ_ε ≥ μ(K) − 2η − δ_ε > t + 2η − δ_ε > t for small ε. With step 3 this is (i).
5. spt T = U ∖ Z (GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11), Z the union of the open W with W̄ ⊆ U compact and T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ W; x ∈ spt μ iff μ(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ lay in such a W, then M_W(T) = 0, so μ(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ; so U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ, take r > 0 with μ(B_r(x)) = 0, B̄_r(x) ⊆ U; by step 2 T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), so x ∈ Z, x ∉ spt T. Hence (ii).
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., and ξ^♭ satisfies |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩.
Integral formula T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Upper bound: admissible ω give T(ω) ≤ μ(W), so M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
Lower bound: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, cutoff and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) > t for each real t < μ(W).
Support: by (i) and the integral formula, the zero region Z of T is U ∖ spt μ, so spt T = U ∩ spt μ.

subproblems.title: Passing a measure inequality from compactly contained open neighbourhoods to a compact set (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, E ⊆ U compact, μ and ν measures on ℝ^P with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and c ∈ [0, ∞]. Suppose μ(G) ≤ ν(G) + c for every open G ⊇ E such that closure(G) is compact and contained in U. Then μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.compact_outer_bound-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U E : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (c : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → IsCompact E → E ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ν K < ∞) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → E ⊆ G → CompactlyContained G U → μ G ≤ ν G + c) → μ E ≤ ν E + c
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by compact_sum_bound (step 5), which applies it in the open set U′ ⊆ U with c = 0, as step 4 of the selected parent's proof does for Σ = F ∖ W.
Source: Simon 7.2.4 (10), chapter-07.txt lines 245–256: an inequality between masses on open neighbourhoods W_γ, γ ↓ α, is passed to the limit set by continuity from above of a measure that is finite near it. Its audited proof (supplied for root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.compact_outer_bound-a1) follows.

1. If E = ∅ then μ(E) = 0 and there is nothing to prove; the argument below also covers this case. Choose δ > 0 with C_δ := {x : dist(x, E) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := δ/(k + 2) ∈ (0, δ) and G_k := {x : dist(x, E) < r_k} (open thickening).
2. Each G_k is open and contains E (r_k > 0). closure(G_k) ⊆ {dist(·, E) ≤ r_k} ⊆ C_δ ⊆ U, and C_δ is compact (closed thickening of a compact set in the proper space ℝ^P), so closure(G_k) is compact and contained in U. By hypothesis and monotonicity, μ(E) ≤ μ(G_k) ≤ ν(G_k) + c for every k.
3. Since r_k decreases, (G_k) is decreasing. ⋂_k G_k = E: E ⊆ G_k for all k; conversely, if dist(x, E) < r_k for all k, then for every ε > 0 some r_k < ε gives x ∈ {dist(·, E) < ε}, so x ∈ ⋂_{ε>0} {dist(·, E) < ε} = closure(E) (Metric.closure_eq_iInter_thickening) = E, E being compact and hence closed. The G_k are open, hence measurable, and ν(G_0) ≤ ν(C_δ) < ∞.
4. By continuity from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), ν(G_k) → ν(E). Addition of the constant c is continuous on [0, ∞], so ν(G_k) + c → ν(E) + c, and letting k → ∞ in μ(E) ≤ ν(G_k) + c gives μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c. ∎
proof_key_steps: δ > 0 with closed δ-thickening of E inside U; G_k := open δ/(k + 2)-thickening of E.
Each G_k is open, contains E and has compact closure in U, so μ(E) ≤ μ(G_k) ≤ ν(G_k) + c.
G_k decreases to closure(E) = E and ν(G_0) < ∞; continuity from above gives ν(G_k) → ν(E), hence μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c.

subproblems.title: Local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M and of the weight of an integer multiplicity representation (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (an IMRep U n). That is: M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M; and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n = μHE[n]. Let μ_R = R.measure = θ·(H^n⌞M), i.e. (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: H^n(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞ and μ_R(K) ≠ ∞ (that is, both are < ∞). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.imrep_local_finiteness-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by compact_sum_bound (step 2, second conjunct). Its second conjunct is exactly preliminary 0(d) of the selected parent's proof (μ_{R′}(K) < ∞ for an IMRep R′ in V and compact K ⊆ V, via withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict and locallyIntegrable_mult). Its audited proof follows.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733-747): the multiplicity θ is a locally H^n-integrable positive integer-valued function. In the frozen contract it is encoded by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult.

Notation: H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P (Euclid P); M = R.carrier; θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ ⊆ [0, ∞]; μ_R = R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U.

1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel (IsCompact.measurableSet).

2. (Weight of K.) Since K is measurable:
- μ_R(K) = ∫_K θ d(H^n⌞M) by the definition of withDensity (withDensity_apply);
- (H^n⌞M)⌞K = H^n⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict).
Hence μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n, after commuting the intersection.

3. The IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n ≠ ∞. By step 2, μ_R(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.

4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K, the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ. Hence 1 ≤ R.mult x, and after casting to [0, ∞], 1 ≤ θ(x).

5. (Measurability.) θ is measurable. It is the composition of the measurable map R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (field measurable_mult) with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).

6. (Unweighted measure.) H^n(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dH^n (setLIntegral_one). This is at most ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n by monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono), using the pointwise bound of step 4 on M ∩ K and the measurability of step 5. The right side is finite by step 3, so H^n(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞. This is the first conclusion. ∎

It was placed after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` in the child comparator scope, i.e. inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` with the frozen contract's `open` commands, after the contract's `noncomputable section ... end`. `exact Submission.rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top` closes the frozen type, and `#print axioms` reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

```lean
theorem Submission.rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞ := by
  intro P n U R K hK hKU
  have hint := R.locallyIntegrable_mult K hK hKU
  have hmeas : R.measure K = ∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ K, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n] := by
    rw [IMRep.measure, withDensity_apply _ hK.measurableSet,
      Measure.restrict_restrict hK.measurableSet, inter_comm]
  refine ⟨?_, by rw [hmeas]; exact hint⟩
  refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top hint ?_
  calc μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) = ∫⁻ _ in R.carrier ∩ K, (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n] := by
        rw [setLIntegral_one]
    _ ≤ ∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ K, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n] := by
        refine setLIntegral_mono (measurable_from_nat.comp R.measurable_mult) ?_
        intro x hx
        exact_mod_cast R.mult_pos x hx.1
```
proof_key_steps: A compact K is closed, hence Borel.
μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n by withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict. This is finite by locallyIntegrable_mult.
θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos) gives H^n(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞.

subproblems.title: Local mass triangle inequality for currents on nested domains (the inline supremum arguments of parent steps 2–4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, V₁, V₂, G ⊆ ℝ^P with U ⊆ V₁ and U ⊆ V₂. Let Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U), X ∈ 𝒟_n(V₁) and Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V₂) be currents (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn), and let c ∈ ℝ. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) let ι₁ω := testFormOnInclusion (U ⊆ V₁) n ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V₁) and ι₂ω := testFormOnInclusion (U ⊆ V₂) n ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V₂) be ω regarded as a test form in the larger domain (same underlying differential form). Suppose Z(ω) = X(ι₁ω) + c·Y(ι₂ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + ofReal(|c|)·M_G(Y) in [0, ∞]. Here M_G(A) = A.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(A(η)) over the test forms η of the domain of A with tsupport η ⊆ G and Euclidean coefficient norm |η(x)| ≤ 1 for every x (covectorEuclideanNorm; massAdmissibleOn), ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, and the product is taken in [0, ∞] (so 0·∞ = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V₁ V₂ G : Set (Euclid P)) (h₁ : U ⊆ V₁) (h₂ : U ⊆ V₂) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (X : GeometricCurrentOn V₁ n) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn V₂ n) (c : ℝ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → Z ω = X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω) + c * Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)) → Z.massOn G ≤ X.massOn G + ENNReal.ofReal |c| * Y.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the supremum arguments that the selected parent's proof writes out inline. Step 2 has Z(ω) = T(ω) for forms supported in O′ = B ∖ F. Step 3 has Z(ω) = S(ω′) − Sr(ω′) = S(ω′) + Sr(−ω′) on W, with the reflected form −ω′ admissible by covectorEuclideanNorm_neg. Step 4 has Z(ω) = T(ω) + Ŷ(ω′) on G′ and ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) + ofReal(Ŷ(ω′)) ≤ M_{G′}(T) + M_{G′}(Ŷ). These are the cases c = 0, c = −1 and c = 1 of the present statement: (V₁, V₂) = (U, ℝ^P) for c = 0 and c = 1, and (V₁, V₂) = (ℝ^P, ℝ^P) for c = −1, where massOn_mono then gives M_W(Sr) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(Sr) = M(Sr). In Simon 7.2.4 (chapter-07.txt lines 223–243) this is the elementary mass inequality M_{W_α}(T + X) ≥ M_{W_α}(T_j + X + ∂R̃_j) − M(S̃_j) that precedes (9). Only the definition of local mass is used; no sibling is needed.
Notation. |·| denotes both the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm on n-covectors and the absolute value on ℝ. For a current A in a domain V, a test form η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) is admissible for M_G(A) if tsupport η ⊆ G and |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn V n G). By definition M_G(A) is the supremum of ofReal(A(η)) over the admissible η. Hence ofReal(A(η)) ≤ M_G(A) for every admissible η (le_massOn), and M_G(A) ≤ s for s ∈ [0, ∞] as soon as ofReal(A(η)) ≤ s for every admissible η (sSup_le).
1. (Reduction.) By sSup_le it suffices to fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) admissible for M_G(Z), i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and to prove ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ M_G(X) + ofReal(|c|)·M_G(Y).
2. (The included forms are admissible.) Put ω₁ := ι₁ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V₁) and ω₂ := ι₂ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V₂). The inclusion does not change the underlying differential form (testFormOnInclusion_coe: the form of ιω is the form of ω). Hence tsupport ω₁ = tsupport ω₂ = tsupport ω ⊆ G, and |ω₁(x)| = |ω₂(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. So ω₁ is admissible for M_G(X) and ω₂ is admissible for M_G(Y).
3. (The reflected form is admissible.) −ω₂ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V₂) has underlying form −ω. Its tsupport is tsupport ω ⊆ G (tsupport_neg). Also |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, because the coefficient norm satisfies |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). So −ω₂ is admissible for M_G(Y).
4. (Evaluation bounds.) By steps 2, 3 and le_massOn: ofReal(X(ω₁)) ≤ M_G(X), ofReal(Y(ω₂)) ≤ M_G(Y) and ofReal(Y(−ω₂)) ≤ M_G(Y). Y is linear, so Y(−ω₂) = −Y(ω₂) (map_neg). The real number |Y(ω₂)| equals Y(ω₂) or −Y(ω₂) (abs_cases). In both cases ofReal(|Y(ω₂)|) ≤ M_G(Y).
5. (Pointwise estimate.) The hypothesis applies because tsupport ω ⊆ G: Z(ω) = X(ω₁) + c·Y(ω₂). For real numbers, c·y ≤ |c·y| = |c|·|y| (le_abs_self, abs_mul), so Z(ω) ≤ X(ω₁) + |c|·|Y(ω₂)|. ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). Moreover ofReal(p + q) ≤ ofReal(p) + ofReal(q) for all real p, q (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le), and ofReal(|c|·|y|) = ofReal(|c|)·ofReal(|y|) because |c| ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Hence ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω₁)) + ofReal(|c|)·ofReal(|Y(ω₂)|).
6. (Conclusion.) Addition and multiplication by the fixed factor ofReal(|c|) are monotone on [0, ∞]. So by step 4 the right side of step 5 is at most M_G(X) + ofReal(|c|)·M_G(Y). This is the claim of step 1. Taking the supremum over all admissible ω (sSup_le) gives M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + ofReal(|c|)·M_G(Y). ∎
Remark (not part of the proof). ofReal(|c|) = 1 for c = ±1, and ofReal(|0|)·M_G(Y) = 0 even when M_G(Y) = ∞. So the cases used by the parent read M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y) for c = ±1 and M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) for c = 0.
Appendix (verified Lean realization of the numbered proof above; not part of the proof). The declaration below compiles with Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c and SimonGMT 2b366308. It was placed after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` in the child comparator scope (inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` with the frozen contract's `open` commands, after its `noncomputable section ... end`). `exact Submission.dimred_mbl_lc_ic_rb_massOn_le_add_incl` closes the frozen type, and `#print axioms` reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
```lean
theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_lc_ic_rb_massOn_le_add_incl : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V₁ V₂ G : Set (Euclid P)) (h₁ : U ⊆ V₁) (h₂ : U ⊆ V₂) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (X : GeometricCurrentOn V₁ n) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn V₂ n) (c : ℝ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → Z ω = X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω) + c * Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)) → Z.massOn G ≤ X.massOn G + ENNReal.ofReal |c| * Y.massOn G := by
  intro P n U V₁ V₂ G h₁ h₂ Z X Y c hZ
  refine sSup_le ?_
  rintro r ⟨ω, hω, rfl⟩
  -- the inclusions keep the underlying form, so they keep admissibility
  have hω₁ : testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V₁ n G := ⟨hω.1, hω.2⟩
  have hω₂ : testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V₂ n G := ⟨hω.1, hω.2⟩
  have hneg : -testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V₂ n G := by
    refine ⟨?_, fun x => ?_⟩
    · have hco : ((-testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω : TestFormOn V₂ n) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) =
          -(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) := rfl
      rw [hco, tsupport_neg]
      exact hω.1
    · have hco : ((-testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω : TestFormOn V₂ n) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x =
          -((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) := rfl
      rw [hco, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg]
      exact hω.2 x
  have hX : ENNReal.ofReal (X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω)) ≤ X.massOn G := X.le_massOn hω₁
  have hY : ENNReal.ofReal (Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)) ≤ Y.massOn G := Y.le_massOn hω₂
  have hY' : ENNReal.ofReal (Y (-testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)) ≤ Y.massOn G := Y.le_massOn hneg
  have hYneg : Y (-testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω) = -Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω) :=
    map_neg Y.toCurrent _
  rw [hYneg] at hY'
  have habs : ENNReal.ofReal |Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)| ≤ Y.massOn G := by
    rcases abs_cases (Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)) with ⟨h, _⟩ | ⟨h, _⟩
    · rw [h]; exact hY
    · rw [h]; exact hY'
  have hcy : c * Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω) ≤ |c| * |Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)| := by
    calc c * Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω) ≤ |c * Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)| := le_abs_self _
      _ = |c| * |Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)| := abs_mul _ _
  show ENNReal.ofReal (Z ω) ≤ X.massOn G + ENNReal.ofReal |c| * Y.massOn G
  calc ENNReal.ofReal (Z ω)
      = ENNReal.ofReal (X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω) + c * Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)) := by
        rw [hZ ω hω.1]
    _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω) + |c| * |Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)|) :=
        ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (by linarith)
    _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω)) +
          ENNReal.ofReal (|c| * |Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)|) := ENNReal.ofReal_add_le
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal (X (testFormOnInclusion h₁ n ω)) +
          ENNReal.ofReal |c| * ENNReal.ofReal |Y (testFormOnInclusion h₂ n ω)| := by
        rw [ENNReal.ofReal_mul (abs_nonneg c)]
    _ ≤ X.massOn G + ENNReal.ofReal |c| * Y.massOn G := by gcongr
```
proof_key_steps: For ω admissible for M_G(Z), the included forms ι₁ω and ι₂ω have the same underlying form as ω, so they are admissible for M_G(X) and M_G(Y); −ι₂ω is admissible too (tsupport_neg, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
le_massOn gives ofReal(X(ι₁ω)) ≤ M_G(X) and, using Y(−ι₂ω) = −Y(ι₂ω), ofReal(|Y(ι₂ω)|) ≤ M_G(Y).
Z(ω) = X(ι₁ω) + c·Y(ι₂ω) ≤ X(ι₁ω) + |c|·|Y(ι₂ω)|; ofReal monotone, ofReal_add_le and ofReal_mul give ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ M_G(X) + ofReal(|c|)·M_G(Y).
Take the supremum over all admissible ω (sSup_le).

subproblems.title: Mass-measure bound on a compact set for Z = T + Y|_U near the set (parent step 4; Simon 7.2.4 (10))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let U′ ⊆ U be open and let E ⊆ U′ be compact. Let T, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n). Let R and R_Z be integer multiplicity representations in U (IMRep U n) with R.Represents T and R_Z.Represents Z, and let R_Y be one in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) with R_Y.Represents Y. Suppose Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ιω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U′, where ιω = testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω is ω regarded as a test form on ℝ^P. Then μ_{R_Z}(E) ≤ μ_R(E) + μ_{R_Y}(E) in [0, ∞], where μ_{R′} := R′.measure = θ′Hⁿ⌞M′ is the weight of R′ = (M′, θ′, ξ′).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U U' E : Set (Euclid P)) (T Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R RZ : IMRep U n) (RY : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsOpen U → IsOpen U' → U' ⊆ U → IsCompact E → E ⊆ U' → R.Represents T → RZ.Represents Z → RY.Represents Y → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ U' → Z ω = T ω + Y (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω)) → RZ.measure E ≤ R.measure E + RY.measure E
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the selected parent's proof (region Σ = F ∖ W; parent 8(c)). There the open set is U′ = U ∖ spt(S − C), the compact set is Σ and Y is Ŷ. Here they are an arbitrary open U′ ⊆ U, a compact E ⊆ U′ and any represented Y. This is Simon 7.2.4 (10) (chapter-07.txt lines 245–256): an inequality between masses on open neighbourhoods is passed to the limit set by letting the neighbourhoods shrink. Siblings used: (MR) mass_and_support, part (i): if R′ represents a current A in an open domain, then M_G(A) = μ_{R′}(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P. (COB) compact_outer_bound. (FIN) imrep_local_finiteness, second conjunct: μ_{R′}(K) ≠ ∞ for every IMRep R′ in a set V and every compact K ⊆ V. (MT) mixed_mass_triangle.
Notation. μ_R = R.measure, μ_{R_Z} = R_Z.measure and μ_{R_Y} = R_Y.measure are measures on ℝ^P. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ιω = testFormOnInclusion (U ⊆ ℝ^P) n ω and ι₀ω := testFormOnInclusion (U ⊆ U) n ω.
1. (Masses on open sets.) U and ℝ^P are open. By (MR)(i) for (T, R) and (Z, R_Z) in U and for (Y, R_Y) in ℝ^P, every open G ⊆ ℝ^P satisfies M_G(T) = μ_R(G), M_G(Z) = μ_{R_Z}(G) and M_G(Y) = μ_{R_Y}(G).
2. (Local finiteness.) Let ν := μ_R + μ_{R_Y}, a measure on ℝ^P with ν(A) = μ_R(A) + μ_{R_Y}(A) for all A (Measure.add_apply). Let K ⊆ U′ be compact. Then K ⊆ U because U′ ⊆ U, so μ_R(K) ≠ ∞ by (FIN) for the IMRep R in U. Also K ⊆ ℝ^P, so μ_{R_Y}(K) ≠ ∞ by (FIN) for the IMRep R_Y in ℝ^P. Hence ν(K) < ∞ (ENNReal.add_lt_top).
3. (The identity on a neighbourhood.) Let G be open with E ⊆ G and CompactlyContained G U′, i.e. closure(G) is compact and closure(G) ⊆ U′. Then G ⊆ closure(G) ⊆ U′. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then tsupport ω ⊆ U′, so by hypothesis Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ιω). Now ι₀ω has the same underlying form as ω and lies in the same space 𝒟ⁿ(U); elements of 𝒟ⁿ(U) are determined by their underlying form, so ι₀ω = ω. Hence Z(ω) = T(ι₀ω) + 1·Y(ιω).
4. (Bound on the neighbourhood.) Apply (MT) with the domains U ⊆ V₁ := U and U ⊆ V₂ := ℝ^P, the currents Z, X := T and Y, and c := 1. Its hypothesis is step 3. Since ofReal(|1|) = 1, it gives M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(T) + M_G(Y). G is open, so step 1 turns this into μ_{R_Z}(G) ≤ μ_R(G) + μ_{R_Y}(G) = ν(G) + 0.
5. (Passage to E.) Apply (COB) with the open set U′, the compact set E ⊆ U′, the measures μ := μ_{R_Z} and ν, and the constant c := 0. Its finiteness hypothesis is step 2 and its neighbourhood hypothesis is step 4. It gives μ_{R_Z}(E) ≤ ν(E) + 0 = μ_R(E) + μ_{R_Y}(E). ∎

```lean
theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_lc_ic_rb_measure_le_add_of_compact : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U U' E : Set (Euclid P)) (T Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R RZ : IMRep U n) (RY : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsOpen U → IsOpen U' → U' ⊆ U → IsCompact E → E ⊆ U' → R.Represents T → RZ.Represents Z → RY.Represents Y → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ U' → Z ω = T ω + Y (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω)) → RZ.measure E ≤ R.measure E + RY.measure E := by
  intro P n U U' E T Z Y R RZ RY hU hU' hU'U hE hEU' hR hRZ hRY hZ
  have hMT := (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support P n U T R hU hR).1
```
